correctness.rationale: The vertex set is a published consequence of polarity for the optimization balls. The proof independently characterizes exposed one-dimensional faces by the kth absolute coefficient tie, giving adjacency exactly when the dot product is k-1. A monotone target-match invariant supplies the lower bounds, and explicit exchange chains attain them in both support-different and same-support cases. The shell count is a direct partition by same-sign, opposite-sign, and exchanged coordinates. Exhaustive BFS through dimension seven reproduces every pair distance, degree, diameter, and shell size.

value.rationale: These polytopes are optimization norm balls whose combinatorics was introduced specifically with algorithmic and monotone-path motivations. The result gives their complete one-skeleton metric, sharp diameter, and distance distribution in closed form, turning a face-enumeration description into exact navigational geometry. It also identifies the optimization-ball skeleton with the signed Johnson graph now used in coding and kissing-arrangement work. The result is structural rather than a small finite table or arbitrary parameter slice.
